cues.en: An electric car’s battery pack doesn’t have a capacity in gallons, of course, but it does have a capacity.

cues.zh: 我们不用液体化学混合物的体积来表示这个容量，
cues.en: Rather than giving that capacity in volume of a liquid chemical concoction,

cues.zh: 而是用原始能量的单位来定义它的容量。
cues.en: we define its capacity in raw energy terms.

cues.zh: 能量，它让世界运转起来！
cues.en: Energy. It makes the world go ‘round!

cues.en: But what is it really?

cues.zh: 这一节会感觉我们深入到了细枝末节，但这对理解充电原理至关重要。
cues.en: This section is going to feel like we’re deep in the weeds but it’s fundamental to understanding how charging works.

cues.zh: 首先，你需要理解功率和能量的区别。
cues.en: First, you need to understand the difference between power and energy.

cues.zh: 这一点让很多人困惑，因为确实有点绕。
cues.en: This trips a lot of folks up because it’s a bit confusing.

cues.zh: 你可能对生活中各种东西的功率有个大致概念，
cues.en: You probably have a general sense of how much power things in your life use,

cues.zh: 比如灯泡都标有瓦数。
cues.en: for instance light bulbs are given a wattage.

cues.zh: 不过，瓦特是瞬时功率的单位，不是能量。
cues.en: The watt, though, is a unit of instantaneous power, not energy.

cues.zh: 从功率计算能量需要一个时间分量，
cues.en: Quantifying energy from power requires a time component,

cues.zh: 在电学领域，我们使用瓦时。
cues.en: and in the realm of electricity we use the watt-hour.

cues.zh: 瓦时就是字面意思。
cues.en: Watt-hours are what they sound like.

cues.zh: 它就是一小时内平均功率消耗的瓦数。
cues.en: It’s simply the average power draw in watts that occurs over a period of one hour.

cues.zh: 举个例子，一个10瓦的灯泡运行1小时，会消耗10瓦时的能量。
cues.en: As an example, a 10 watt light bulb that has run for 1 hour will have consumed 10 watt-hours of energy.

cues.zh: 当你改变功率水平时，就改变了能量消耗的速度。
cues.en: When you change the power level, you change the speed at which energy is consumed.

cues.zh: 功率更高的灯泡会更快地消耗能量。
cues.en: A more powerful light bulb will burn through energy more quickly.

cues.zh: 比如一个100瓦的灯泡只需运行6分钟，就能消耗掉同样的10瓦时，
cues.en: For instance a one hundred watt light bulb only needs to run for six minutes to have consumed the same 10 watt-hours

cues.zh: 和我们那个10瓦灯泡运行一小时一样。
cues.en: as our 10 watt bulb does over an hour.

cues.zh: 它的功率是10倍，所以达到相同的总能量消耗只需十分之一的时间。
cues.en: It uses 10 times as much power, so the same total energy use is reached in one tenth the time.

cues.zh: 瓦时其实很小，所以在谈论电能时
cues.en: Watt-hours are pretty small, though, so when talking about electrical energy

cues.zh: 我们通常用千瓦时——也就是一千瓦时。
cues.en: we usually use the kilowatt-hour - which is just one thousand watt-hours.

cues.zh: 你的电力公司很可能用这个单位给你计费。
cues.en: Your electric utility probably bills you in this unit.

cues.zh: 而电动汽车的电池组容量也是用千瓦时来表示的。
cues.en: And the battery pack capacity of an electric car is given in kilowatt-hours.

cues.zh: 目前市场上的纯电动汽车（指的是纯电动的，不是混合动力系统）
cues.en: Battery-electric vehicles on the market today (meaning those which are purely electric, not hybrid powertrains)

cues.zh: 通常电池组容量至少为30千瓦时，不过在美国市场上50千瓦时以上更为常见。
cues.en: usually have battery packs of at least 30 kilowatt-hours, though 50+ is more typical in the US market.

cues.zh: 许多车型提供不同容量的电池组可供选择，
cues.en: Many models are available with different pack sizes to choose from,

cues.zh: 比如我的车——现代Ioniq 5——基础配置可选58千瓦时的电池组，
cues.en: for instance my car - a Hyundai Ioniq 5 - can be had with either a 58 kWh pack in its base configuration,

cues.zh: 或者77.4千瓦时的电池组，也就是我这款的容量。
cues.en: or a 77.4 kWh pack, the size I have.

cues.zh: 值得注意的是，目前汽车制造商往往有点含糊
cues.en: Of note, right now, car manufacturers tend to be a little vague

cues.zh: 他们给电池组标的数据到底是电池组的实际容量还是可用容量。
cues.en: on whether the figure they give their battery packs is the pack’s actual capacity or a usable capacity.

cues.zh: 你看，为了延长电池寿命，大多数车只让你使用电池组电量水平中的特定范围。
cues.en: See, to prolong battery life most cars only give you access to a certain range of the pack’s charge levels.

cues.zh: 把电池电芯推到极限会加剧电池单元的磨损，
cues.en: It puts more wear and tear on a battery cell when you push it to its extremes,

cues.zh: 所以比较典型的情况是，显示100%充电实际上大约是95%的电量，
cues.en: so somewhat typical is for a 100% indicated charge to really be something like a 95% charge,

cues.zh: 而当电池在显示0%时“没电”了，实际上大约还有5%的电量。
cues.en: and when the battery is “dead” at an indicated 0%, it’s really more like 5% charged still.

cues.zh: 需要说明的是，这是个好做法！
cues.en: To be clear, this is a good practice!

cues.zh: 但我希望每个制造商都能为他们的电池组提供明确的总容量和可用容量指标
cues.en: But I wish every manufacturer would give distinct gross and usable capacity metrics for their battery packs

cues.zh: 这样我们就能了解他们把电芯压榨到了什么程度。
cues.en: so we can understand how much they’re pushing the cells.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，很多电动车允许你设置最高充电量，这样就能更温和地对待电池。
cues.en: For what it’s worth, many EVs will let you be gentler on their batteries by allowing you to set a maximum charge level.

cues.zh: 我把车设定在80%就停止充电，因为说实话它的续航远超我的需求，
cues.en: I have my car set to stop charging at 80% because honestly it has way more range than I need,

cues.zh: 而且限制充电上限被认为能延长电池组寿命。
cues.en: and limiting charge levels is thought to prolong battery pack life.

cues.zh: 总之，回到我刚才说的。
cues.en: Anyway, let’s go back to what I said earlier.

cues.zh: 电池组就是新的油箱，千瓦时就是新的加仑。
cues.en: The battery pack is the new gas tank, and the kilowatt-hour is the new gallon.

cues.zh: 所以，我这辆车的“油箱”容量是77.4 kWh。
cues.en: So, my car’s “tank” holds 77.4 kWh.

cues.en: And how many miles can each of those 77.4 kWh take me?

cues.en: This car, like lots out there, actually gives you efficiency in miles per kilowatt-hour,

cues.zh: 就像每加仑英里数一样，数值越高越好。
cues.en: and just like miles per gallon, a higher number is better.

cues.zh: 有些车会反过来，告诉你行驶一英里消耗多少瓦时，
cues.en: Some cars will flip that and tell you how many watt-hours you consume to go a mile,

cues.en: but I find distance-driven per kilowatt-hour to be much more human-friendly,

cues.en: especially since I pay for electricity in that unit.

cues.en: How far can a full “tank” take me, then?

cues.zh: 3（即每千瓦时能量能跑的距离）
cues.en: 3 (our distance we can go with a kWh of energy)

cues.en: highway driving is less efficient than stop-and-go.

cues.zh: 电量超过80%后，充电速度会大幅下降，这是物理和化学原因导致的，
cues.en: Beyond 80% state of charge, charging speed drops quite a lot because, for physics and chemistry reasons,

cues.zh: 把电子推入电池单元变得困难得多。
cues.en: it becomes a lot harder to push electrons into the battery cells.

cues.zh: 我见过一些人纠结这一点，甚至认为这是汽车制造商某种作弊或虚假宣传，但是，
cues.en: I’ve seen a few folks fixate on this and even view it as some sort of cheating or false advertising on the part of automakers but,

cues.zh: 事情是这样的。
cues.en: well here’s the thing.

cues.zh: 你其实不需要每次都充满。
cues.en: You don’t actually need to top up every time you charge.

cues.zh: 为了最后20%的电量浪费时间很不值，毕竟100英里外就有另一个充电桩。
cues.en: It’s a huge waste of your time to get that last 20% when there’s another charger 100 miles away.

cues.zh: 当然，由于每次停靠实际上只用了70%的续航，你会需要更频繁地充电，
cues.en: Sure, you’ll end up needing to charge more frequently since you’ll effectively only be using 70% of your range between stops,

cues.zh: 但我的车这样也还能跑170多英里。
cues.en: but in my car that’s still over 170 miles.

cues.zh: 每开两个半小时就停下来充20分钟电，其实远没有你想的那么糟。
cues.en: Stopping for a 20 minute charge after every two and a half hours of driving isn’t nearly as bad as you might think.

cues.zh: 我还挺享受的，
cues.en: I legitimately quite enjoyed it,

cues.zh: 不过说实话，我的车充电特别快。
cues.en: though to be fair my car charges exceptionally quickly.

cues.zh: 但如果充电同样快的车型不能很快成为主流，我会很意外。
cues.en: I’d be very surprised if just-as-fast-to-charge models don’t become the norm pretty quickly, though.

cues.zh: 很多电动车会在导航软件里帮你规划路线，
cues.en: Many EVs will help you plan a route in their navigation software

cues.zh: 根据电池组的充电曲线，优化在充电站所需的最短时间，
cues.en: which optimizes for the least time required at chargers based on their battery pack’s charging curve,

cues.zh: 当然，如果你愿意，也可以用 A Better Route Planner 这类应用自己折腾。
cues.en: although you can also play around with apps such as A Better Route Planner if you’d like.

cues.zh: 或者，如果你的车像我的一样……
cues.en: Or if, like me, you have a car which just…

cues.zh: 完全帮不上路线规划的忙。
cues.en: doesn’t help with route planning.

cues.zh: 不过我倒不太介意我的车缺了这个功能，
cues.en: I’m not too bummed by my car’s omission there, though,

cues.zh: 因为我完全预期高速公路沿线的直流快充站会迅速普及，让这种提前规划变得没那么必要。
cues.en: because I fully expect DC fast charging stations along highway corridors to proliferate pretty quickly, and make that sort of planning ahead less necessary.

cues.zh: 不过，我的车还有一件事做不到，至少目前还不行，而这件事它绝对需要：
cues.en: However, there is one thing my car doesn’t really do, at least not yet, that it absolutely needs to:

cues.zh: 电池预热。
cues.en: battery preconditioning.

cues.zh: 如今的电池化学特性在特定温度范围内表现最佳。
cues.en: Today’s battery chemistries are happiest within a certain temperature range.

cues.zh: 市面上几乎每辆电动车——甚至初代 Chevy Volt——都有办法加热和冷却电池包，让它保持在最佳状态。
cues.en: Nearly every EV on the market - even the original Chevy Volt - has means to heat and cool the battery pack to keep it in its happy place.

cues.zh: 但在直流快充时，要想达到最快速度，电芯需要相当温暖——
cues.en: But when DC fast charging, to get the fastest possible speeds the battery cells need to be pretty warm -

cues.zh: 比平时行驶所需的温度还要高。
cues.en: warmer than they otherwise need to be to drive.

cues.zh: 而在冬天，如果电池不够暖，直流快充可能会……
cues.en: And in the winter, if the battery isn’t warm enough DC fast charging may be…

cues.zh: 没那么快。
cues.en: not so fast.

cues.zh: 至少一开始不会。一旦车辆意识到自己接上了快充桩，就会尽快给电池包加热，
cues.en: At least, not at first. Once the car realizes it’s on a fast charger it’ll start heating the pack up as fast as it can,

cues.zh: 但电池实在太大，这可能需要一段时间。
cues.en: but since the battery is so massive, that can take a while.

cues.zh: 天气冷的时候，你很容易看到充电时间增加20到30分钟。
cues.en: You could easily see a 20 to 30 minute increase in charging time when it’s cold out.

cues.zh: 某些电动车，尤其是特斯拉和少数其他品牌，会开始消耗能量来给电池包预热
cues.en: Certain EVs, notably Teslas and a few others as well, will start expending energy to warm up their battery packs

cues.zh: 当你接近直流快充站时。
cues.en: as you approach a DC fast charger.

cues.zh: 这种电池预热让它们一插上就能接受最大功率，或者至少接近最大功率。
cues.en: This battery preconditioning allows them to accept maximum power, or close to it anyway, as soon as it’s plugged in.

cues.zh: 在我看来，这是一个需要推广到所有电动车的重要功能。
cues.en: This is an important feature that needs to roll out to all EVs, in my opinion.

cues.zh: 坦白说，我不在乎它是否像特斯拉或保时捷的实现那样花哨，能知道你因为导航去快充站而正前往那里——
cues.en: Frankly I don’t care if it’s as fancy as Tesla's or Porsche’s implementation where it knows you’re headed to a fast charger because you’re navigating to one -

cues.zh: 事实上，作为一个用 Android Auto 上的 Waze 导航的人，我有点不喜欢那样。
cues.en: as a matter of fact I kinda don’t like that as someone who navigates with Waze using Android Auto.

cues.zh: 我宁愿只是一个我能按的按钮，或者一句我能下的语音指令
cues.en: I’d rather there just be a button I can press or a voice command I can give

cues.zh: 当我在距离下一个充电站大约15英里的时候。
cues.en: when I’m 15 miles or so from the next charger.

cues.zh: 不过我很欣赏这些自动化方案能防止我忘记操作。
cues.en: But I do appreciate how the automated schemes would keep me from forgetting to do that.

cues.zh: 话虽如此，如今 DC 快充最大的问题
cues.en: With all this said, the biggest issue with DC fast charging today

cues.zh: 是我们现在的充电桩数量勉强够用。
cues.en: is that we barely have enough chargers right now.

cues.zh: 一些热门路线已经出现排队充电的情况，而且随着电动车销量增加，这还会更糟。
cues.en: Already some popular corridors are experiencing charging queues, and this will get worse as more EVs are sold.

cues.zh: 好消息当然是，电动车卖得越多，对充电桩的需求就越大，
cues.en: The good news of course is more EVs that are sold means there’s more demand for chargers,

cues.zh: 但我们正处在成长的阵痛期。
cues.en: but we’re in the midst of growing pains.

cues.zh: 比如，充电桩的可靠性越来越让人担忧，有些网络运营商在运营自家网络方面做得并不怎么样。
cues.en: Like, for instance, charger reliability is a growing concern, and some network operators are less-than-great at operating their networks.

cues.zh: 我个人认为，这在很大程度上是因为 DC 快充技师目前是个非常稀缺的岗位，
cues.en: My personal belief is that a lot of this comes from the fact that DC fast charging technician is a very rare job title right now,

cues.zh: 再加上现有充电桩分布稀疏，
cues.en: and with the current makeup of sparsely-spaced chargers,

cues.zh: 当它们需要零件或维修时，赶到现场是件麻烦事。
cues.en: getting to them when they need parts or repair is a chore.

cues.zh: 我不是想拿这个当借口，但这确实让我相当确信，随着时间推移情况会好转。
cues.en: I don’t mean to use this as an excuse, but it does make me fairly confident this will get better with time.

cues.zh: 不过我们先放下直流快充
cues.en: But let’s move on from DC fast charging

cues.zh: 最后再讲几个影响续航里程的因素。
cues.en: and finish up with some pointers on factors which affect your driving range.

cues.zh: ♫ 音乐 ♫
cues.en: ♫ Music ♫

cues.zh: 我已经提过几次了，但如果你住在寒冷的地方，冬天续航里程会下降。
cues.en: I’ve brought it up a few times already but if you live in a cold place, in winter driving range drops.

cues.zh: 我很想告诉你只是降一点点，但遗憾的是，降幅可能相当可观。
cues.en: And I’d like to tell you it’s just a little bit, but unfortunately it can be significant.

cues.zh: 不过我要再次强调，以今天的电动车而言，
cues.en: I do want to stress again, though, that with today’s EVs,

cues.zh: 只要你的通勤距离合理，而且家里能用充电桩，这些续航损失不太会影响你的日常需求。
cues.en: so long as your commute is reasonable and you have access to a charger at home, these range losses are unlikely to impact your day to day needs.

cues.zh: 它们会延长充电时间，让你在充电上多花一点钱，
cues.en: They will extend charging time and cause you to spend a little more money on charging,

cues.zh: 但当你每天平均只开40甚至80英里时，这不算什么大问题。
cues.en: but when you are only driving an average of 40 or even 80 miles a day, it’s not a big deal.

cues.zh: 不过，长途驾驶确实有一些挑战。
cues.en: Long distance driving does have some challenges, though.

cues.zh: 你可能会问，为什么会出现这种低温续航衰减？
cues.en: You might want to ask, why does this cold-weather range loss happen?

cues.zh: 其实，续航衰减的很大一部分来自座舱取暖。
cues.en: Well, a huge part of the range loss comes from using the cabin heat.

cues.zh: 在燃油车里，引擎盖下那台“爆炸机器”把化学能转化为机械能的效率太差，
cues.en: In a combustion vehicle, the explodey machine under the hood is so bad at turning chemical energy into mechanical energy

cues.zh: 结果产生大量废热，还得想办法排掉。
cues.en: that it ends up with all this waste heat it needs to get rid of.

cues.zh: 每分钟真的会发生上千次爆炸，而爆炸是热的。
cues.en: There’s literal explosions happening over a thousand times per minute, and explosions are hot.

cues.zh: 处理这些热量正是汽车的冷却系统和散热器的职责，
cues.en: Dealing with that heat is what the car’s cooling system and radiator is for,

cues.zh: 通过把第二路发动机冷却液引入座舱，流经一个叫暖风芯体的小散热器，
cues.en: and by running a second circuit of engine coolant into the cabin and through a small radiator called the heater core,

cues.zh: 燃烧产生的多余热量就能用来给你取暖。
cues.en: the excess heat from the combustion can be used to keep you warm.

cues.zh: 否则这些热量就白白浪费了，所以它是免费的热量。
cues.en: Since it would otherwise be wasted, it’s free heat.

cues.zh: 不过，电动汽车几乎不产生什么废热。
cues.en: Electric vehicles, though, don’t produce much waste heat at all.

cues.zh: 这很酷！这正是全世界都为它们兴奋的原因，
cues.en: This is cool! It’s why the world is excited about them,

cues.zh: 它们能效要高得多得多。
cues.en: they’re just much, much, much more energy-efficient.

cues.zh: 但这也意味着，当你想给车厢供暖时，就得从电池包里取电。
cues.en: But that means that when you want to warm the cabin, you have to take energy out of the battery pack.

cues.zh: 这样一来，留给驱动车辆的电量就更少了。
cues.en: And that leaves you with less for driving the car.

cues.zh: 对于配备电阻式车厢加热器的电动汽车，大约到仲秋时节你就会开始注意到续航下降。
cues.en: With an EV that has a resistive cabin heater, you’ll start to notice range dropping around mid-fall.

cues.zh: 基本上就是你一开始需要用加热器的时候。
cues.en: Basically as soon as you start needing to use the heater.

cues.zh: 起初还比较轻微，但一旦进入真正的冬季月份，你可以预期大约30%的续航损失。
cues.en: It will be pretty mild at first, but once you’re into the true winter months, you can expect about 30% range loss.

cues.zh: 我家2017款雪佛兰Bolt，夏天高速续航能稳定达到230英里，而从12月到3月初会降到160到170英里之间。
cues.en: My family’s 2017 Chevy Bolt went from reliably hitting 230 miles of highway range in the summer down to between 160 and 170 from December to early March.

cues.zh: 多开座椅加热、少开空调暖气会有帮助，
cues.en: Using seat heaters more and cabin heat less can help,

cues.zh: 但需要除霜时，基本就只能开着暖气了。
cues.en: but whenever you need to use your defroster you’re kinda stuck running the heat.

cues.zh: 除非你用的是那种很酷的直热式挡风玻璃，我觉得这功能该成为电动车的标配！
cues.en: Unless of course you have one of those cool direct-heated windshields, a feature I think should be standard on EVs!

cues.zh: 说到功能，有个功能终于普及到越来越多电动车上了，
cues.en: Speaking of features, one feature that’s finally spreading to more and more EVs is,

cues.zh: 请鼓掌，
cues.en: drumroll please,

cues.zh: 热泵！
cues.en: HEAT PUMPS!

cues.zh: 如果你不熟悉本频道，我超爱热泵。
cues.en: If you’re not familiar with this channel, I love heat pumps.

cues.zh: 它们是最火热的“制冷”神器。
cues.en: They’re the hottest cool things around.

cues.zh: 本质上就是把空调反过来运行，收集并浓缩外界的热能，再送进车内。
cues.en: By doing what essentially amounts to running an air conditioner backwards, you can collect and concentrate heat energy from outside and move it inside.

cues.zh: 既然几乎所有电动车都有空调，
cues.en: And since pretty much every EV out there has air conditioning,

cues.zh: 让它可逆运行显然是顺理成章的下一步。
cues.en: making it reversible was an obvious next step.

cues.zh: 我不知道为什么要花这么长时间。
cues.en: I don't know why it took so long.

cues.zh: 这样做能让电动车把座舱供暖的能耗降低多达75%，
cues.en: Doing this allows an EV to cut its energy consumption for cabin heat by up to 75%,

cues.zh: 因为搬运热量比产生热量要省电得多。
cues.en: as moving heat takes a lot less energy compared to creating heat.

cues.zh: 2022款车型中，现代给四驱版Ioniq 5配备了热泵。
cues.en: For the 2022 model year, Hyundai gave all-wheel-drive Ioniq 5 models a heat pump.

cues.zh: 我希望他们能尽快把它变成标配，因为说实话，这差别可大了。
cues.en: I’m hoping they make that standard soon because let me tell you, it makes a big difference.

cues.zh: 我二月份才提车，所以还没经历过最恶劣的冬季条件，
cues.en: I took delivery of my car in February so I haven’t yet experienced the worst of the worst winter conditions,

cues.zh: 但根据今年早些时候我体验到的情况，冬季续航下降15%到20%似乎挺常见的。
cues.en: but from what I did get to see earlier in the year, a 15 to 20% winter range drop seems fairly typical.

cues.zh: 不过，当天气极冷时，热泵确实需要电阻加热器来补充，所以续航下降幅度可能会更大。
cues.en: When it gets extremely cold, the heat pump does need to be supplemented by a resistive heater so larger range drops are possible, though.

cues.zh: 嗯，我想打消大家的顾虑：就算你堵在路上，甚至更糟，被困在暴风雪里，也不用担心电量耗尽。
cues.en: Oh, and I’d like to dissuade fears of running out of battery juice should you get stuck in traffic or worse stranded in a blizzard.

cues.zh: 车辆行驶时，车内暖风需要更卖力地工作
cues.en: The car’s heater needs to work a lot harder when you’re in motion

cues.zh: 因为迎面而来的风会迅速把车里的热量带走。
cues.en: because all that wind rushing against your car does a great job of sucking heat right out of it.

cues.zh: 但当你减速或停车时，这种情况就不会发生了。至少，不会那么严重。
cues.en: But when you’re slowed or stopped, that’s not happening. At least, not nearly as much.

cues.zh: 在你见过的一些冒险旅程中，那辆雪佛兰Bolt
cues.en: In the Chevy Bolt you’ve seen some adventures in,

cues.zh: 它没有热泵，我注意到在静止状态下，即使气温在零度以下，
cues.en: which doesn’t have a heat pump, I noticed that when stationary, even in subzero temperatures,

cues.zh: 这辆车只消耗1到2千瓦，偶尔会跳到3千瓦，来保持车厢和电池组温暖。
cues.en: the car was only consuming between 1 and 2 kilowatts, with the occasional blip up to 3 kW, to keep the cabin and battery pack warm.

cues.zh: 所以，即使只有三分之一电量，也就是20千瓦时，
cues.en: So, even with only one third battery charge, 20 kWh,

cues.zh: 你可以预期这辆车至少能让你暖和5个小时，可能更久，
cues.en: you could expect that car to keep you warm for at least 5 hours, probably more,

cues.zh: 而且你只要把温度调低、多穿点衣服，就能轻松延长这个时间。
cues.en: and you can easily stretch that just by turning the temperature down and bundling up.

cues.zh: 除了冬天，我们再聊聊还有哪些因素会影响你的续航。
cues.en: Aside from winter, let’s talk about what other things affect your range.

cues.zh: 前面我提到过，高速行驶比走走停停更费电。
cues.en: Earlier I mentioned that highway driving is less efficient than stop-and-go.

cues.zh: 这是为什么呢？
cues.en: Why is that?

cues.zh: 在其他条件都相同的情况下，
cues.en: Well, with all else being equal,

cues.zh: 影响电动车行驶效率的最大单一因素就是你的平均车速。
cues.en: the single greatest factor to driving efficiency in an EV is your average speed.

cues.zh: 你看，车速越快，车子就得费更大的劲才能推开空气前进。
cues.en: See, as you go faster, your car has to work a lot harder to push itself through the air.

cues.zh: 事实上，风阻和滚动阻力基本上就是仅有的两个让车子减速的因素。
cues.en: As a matter of fact, wind resistance and rolling resistance are essentially the only two things working to slow your car.

cues.zh: 两者都会随车速增加而增大，但空气产生的阻力并不是线性关系——
cues.en: Both increase with vehicle speed, but the drag created by air is not a linear function -

cues.zh: 事实上，计算阻力时，速度是要平方的。
cues.en: as a matter of fact when calculating drag force, velocity is squared.

cues.zh: 所以开得越快，电机要把车推动同样的距离就越费劲，
cues.en: So the faster you go, the harder a motor needs to work to push your car the same distance,

cues.zh: 而且车速越高，这种效应越明显。
cues.en: and the effect gets worse as speed increases.

cues.zh: 当然，这并不是电动汽车独有的。
cues.en: That’s not unique to EVs, of course.

cues.zh: 任何车辆都是如此。
cues.en: The same goes for any vehicle.

cues.zh: 但由于车辆在不主动向前推进时不消耗任何能量，
cues.en: But because the vehicle doesn’t use any energy when it’s not actively trying to push itself forward,

cues.zh: 所以不会有怠速发动机那种浪费。
cues.en: you don’t get the waste of an idling engine.

cues.zh: 更妙的是，再生制动能让车在减速或停下时，回收大部分原本用于从静止加速的多余能量。
cues.en: Even better, regenerative braking allows the car to get back most of the excess energy it used to accelerate from a stop

cues.zh: 当你回到停止状态或减速时。
cues.en: when you return to a stop or slow down.

cues.zh: 再生制动和零怠速浪费，使得平均车速基本上成为影响能效的唯一因素。
cues.en: Regen braking and zero idling waste make average vehicle speed essentially the only factor when it comes to energy efficiency.

cues.zh: 当然，这是在讨论风之前。
cues.en: That is of course until we talk about wind.

cues.zh: 当你迎着每小时10英里的逆风行驶时，
cues.en: When you’re driving into a 10 mile an hour headwind,

cues.zh: 风的影响就完全等同于你实际车速比现在快每小时10英里。
cues.en: the effect of the wind is exactly the same as if you were driving 10 miles an hour faster than you really are.

cues.zh: 所以风速会相当显著地影响你的续航里程。
cues.en: So wind conditions can rather drastically affect your driving range.

cues.zh: 在我和 Aging Wheels 一起进行的那次公路旅行中，我们一出发就顶着强劲的逆风行驶，
cues.en: On the road trip I took with Aging Wheels, we started our journey driving right into a nasty headwind,

cues.zh: 这让我这辆车的能效从平时平均每千瓦时 3.2 英里降到了每千瓦时 2.4 英里。
cues.en: which reduced my car’s efficiency from my typical average of 3.2 miles per kWh down to 2.4 miles per kWh.

cues.zh: 这大约让功耗增加了 25%，因此续航里程比我预期的下降了 25%。
cues.en: That was about a 25% increase in power consumption, and thus resulted in a 25% drop in range from what I was expecting.

cues.zh: 最终，这并不算什么问题。
cues.en: In the end, this wasn’t a problem.

cues.zh: 我们的路线规划器设置得太过保守，以至于我们实际能耗几乎正好达到了预期值。
cues.en: Our route planner was being so conservative that we actually hit the expected energy consumption almost exactly.

cues.zh: 另外还有一点要记住，如果我们真的需要延长续航里程，有个非常简单的方法：
cues.en: And, here’s the other thing to keep in mind, if we absolutely needed to stretch our driving range there’s a really easy way to do it:

cues.zh: 减速就行。
cues.en: just slow down.

cues.zh: 由于那股逆风，我们体验到的续航相当于以每小时 90 或 95 英里的速度行驶，
cues.en: Thanks to that head wind, we experienced a range similar to if we were driving perhaps 90 or 95 miles an hour,

cues.zh: 尽管我们实际只开了 70 英里每小时。
cues.en: even though we were really doing 70.

cues.zh: 虽然这显然很烦人，但降到每小时55或60英里会立刻大幅延长我们的续航里程。
cues.en: While it’s obviously annoying, dropping to 55 or 60 miles an hour would immediately have stretched our driving range considerably.

cues.zh: 所以如果其他办法都不管用，那就减速吧。
cues.en: So if all else fails, just slow down.

cues.zh: 风力、平均车速和寒冷天气绝对是影响续航里程的三大因素。
cues.en: Wind, average vehicle speed, and cold weather are definitely the three biggest factors that will impact your driving range.

cues.zh: 但当我开始开电动车时，最让我惊讶的是湿滑路面的影响。
cues.en: But what surprised me the most when I started driving electric was the impact of wet roads.

cues.zh: 小到中雨影响不大，但当雨大到路面积水时，
cues.en: Light to moderate rain doesn’t have too much of an effect, but when it’s raining heavily enough that water is pooling on road surfaces,

cues.zh: 轮胎奋力排开积水所产生的额外阻力，远比我预想的要大得多。
cues.en: the extra drag created as your tires work to push it out of the way is much more substantial than I would have expected.

cues.zh: 就续航而言，最糟糕的驾驶条件是刮风的下雪天加上泥泞湿滑的路面。
cues.en: The absolute worst driving conditions when it comes to range are windy wintry days with slushy road surfaces.

cues.zh: 下足够多的雪，让你一直得开除霜器，这就成了续航大幅缩水的完美配方。
cues.en: Add enough snow to keep you using the defroster and you have a recipe for heavy range loss.

cues.zh: 正因如此，我觉得高速公路沿线需要比现在多得多的直流快充选项，
cues.en: It’s for these reasons that I feel we need much more density in DC fast charging options along highway routes than we currently have

cues.zh: 或者说比我们规划中的多得多。
cues.en: or are planning for.

cues.zh: 间隔50英里是个不错的目标，而且实际上就算续航缩水75%，至少也能让我继续上路。
cues.en: 50 miles apart is a decent target, and realistically even if I had a 75% range loss that would at least keep me on the road.

cues.zh: 但既然实际续航可能比理想情况更难预测，
cues.en: But since driving range can be less predictable than is ideal,

cues.zh: 我希望能看到多得多的直流充电选项。
cues.en: I hope to see far more DC charging options.

cues.zh: 如果我们继续以现在的频率开车跑长途，
cues.en: If we keep driving cars on long trips at the rate we do now,

cues.zh: 最终高速公路沿线的充电站数量就得像今天的加油站一样多。
cues.en: we are eventually going to need as many charging stops along the highway routes as there are gas stations today.

cues.zh: 所以可以肯定，还有很多工作要做。
cues.en: So there’s a lot of work to be done, to be sure.

cues.zh: 但也许我最喜欢电动车的一点是，通常伴随燃料更替而来的先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题被绕开了。
cues.en: But perhaps my favorite thing about electric cars is the chicken-and-egg problem that normally comes with changing fuels is sidestepped.

cues.zh: 有家用充电条件的人，现在就能买电动车。
cues.en: Those of us with home charging can get an electric car right now.

cues.zh: 它能满足我们所有的日常需求，不用依赖公共充电桩。
cues.en: It can take care of all of our daily needs and we don’t need to rely on public charging.

cues.zh: 既然这类车已经存在，高速公路沿线就有了直流快充的市场。
cues.en: And now that those vehicles exist, there’s a market for DC fast charging on highway routes.

cues.zh: 而当今天这些电动车的车主把车卖掉时，市场上会出现更便宜的选项，这会鼓励更多人购买，
cues.en: And when owners of today’s EVs sell them, less expensive options are on the market which encourages more adoption,

cues.zh: 这也会增加压力，推动在公寓小区和其他难以覆盖的区域安装充电设施。
cues.en: and that will increase pressures to install charging infrastructure at apartment complexes and other hard-to-serve areas.

cues.zh: 还有很多工作要做，不少人会说，汽车电动化只是用一个问题换另一个问题。
cues.en: There’s a lot of work to be done, and many would argue that electrifying cars is just trading one problem for another.

cues.zh: 说实话，我越来越不满于我们的基础设施和城市如此以汽车为中心。
cues.en: And to be honest, I’m increasingly upset with how car-centric our infrastructure and cities tend to be.

cues.zh: 但说实话，我现在需要一辆车。
cues.en: But frankly, right now I need a car.

cues.zh: 我不会贬低减少伤害的做法。
cues.en: And I’m not gonna poo poo harm reduction.

cues.zh: 事实是，一旦你弄懂了来龙去脉，转向电动其实相当容易。
cues.en: The fact is going electric is really quite easy once you understand the ins and outs.

cues.en: If you can run a wire to use a dryer you can charge a car and go real far.
